content:
Early voting enters its final week in Webb County on Monday, with five days left for voters to cast a ballot before Election Day. Polls are open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday, Oct. 26, through Friday, Oct. 30, according to the schedule reported by the Laredo Morning Times.

The final week arrives with turnout already running well ahead of the last governor's race. Through the first five days of early voting, Webb County voters cast 20,637 ballots — 20,043 in person and 594 by mail — the Times reported Oct. 23. County Elections Administrator Jose Luis Castillo told KGNS the county is running 20% ahead of the 2022 governor's race, and he projects 40,000 ballots by the end of early voting, with another 30,000 on Election Day.

Monday of the first week was the busiest single day so far, with 5,343 ballots, while Thursday was the slowest at 3,301, the Times reported. The Laredo Fire Department Administrative Center led all polling sites with 6,673 votes through five days.

The ballot carries 38 candidates across 22 contested races at the county, state, and federal levels, plus one proposition, the Times reported. In Texas' 28th Congressional District, incumbent Democrat Henry Cuellar is seeking a 12th term against Republican challenger and Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina and Green Party candidate Marlon Duran. The Laredo mayoral race fields five candidates: incumbent Dr. Victor Trevino, former councilmember Alfonso "Poncho" Casso, District VIII Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa, customs broker Jose David "JD" Gonzalez, and Jorge Garza. Proposition 1 is a non-binding advisory question asking whether the City of Laredo should support efforts to expand pediatric hospital services in the Laredo-Webb County community; it would not authorize a project, funding, or require county action.

The deadline to apply for a mail-in ballot has passed — applications had to arrive by Oct. 23. Mail ballots must be postmarked by Election Day, Nov. 3, and received by 5 p.m. Nov. 4. Texas voters casting a ballot in person must present one of seven acceptable forms of photo ID, or sign a Reasonable Impediment Declaration with an alternative form of ID.

What to watch this week: whether the final five days match the first week's pace and push the county past the administrator's 40,000-ballot projection, and which polling sites draw the heaviest Election Day crowds. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Unlike early voting, Election Day voters must vote in the precinct where they are registered.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "First 5 days of early voting bring more than 20,600 ballots in Webb County," by Jose De La Rosa, Oct. 23, 2026
  • KGNS, "Webb County early voting turnout up 20%, official says," by Ariel Gomez, Oct. 23, 2026
  • VoteTexas.gov, Texas Secretary of State election information

title: Early voting enters its final week in Webb County — five days left to vote early
